root_cause: Ungrounded literals/projections: single-shot generation never checks execution results or real cell values, so guessed string filters, narrow SELECT lists and fragile NOT IN negations go unnoticed
what: Rewrite system_prompt.md with grounding rules (verify literals with LIKE/case-insensitive matching, return all columns for vague 'details'/entity questions, prefer EXCEPT/NOT EXISTS over NOT IN, handle ties), append env.descriptions to the user message, and add a draft-execute-repair control loop in solve.py that uses env.execute to detect errors/empty results and spends the second policy call on a repair prompt containing the error plus sample values from the filtered columns.
decision: s1 delivers a solid +6.67 evolve gain (83.33 -> 90.0) with two fixes and zero regressions, and its grounding/execute-repair mechanism is domain-general rather than task-specific; the ~3x token increase is justified by the measured improvement and it passed the cost rule.

root_cause: No execution feedback loop: drafts that return 0 rows due to unmatched literals or NULL-unsafe NOT IN are shipped unverified
what: Add an execute-and-repair loop: run the draft SQL, and if it errors or returns no rows spend the second policy call on a focused repair prompt that forbids reusing the failed query and points at literal matching (LIKE/case/whitespace), join keys and NULL-safe NOT EXISTS. Add system-prompt rules for NULL-safe negation, literal matching, and projection scope (return full entity rows when the question asks which entities rather than naming an attribute).
decision: cost rule failed: gain +0.0333 within delta 0.0596; shaped -0.334 <= 0

root_cause: Result-shape blindness: drafts that execute with rows are shipped unverified, so wrong projection width (narrow vs SELECT *) and join fan-out duplicates are never repaired
what: Rewrite the projection/duplicate rules in system_prompt.md (vague 'details'/'which entities' => SELECT * over the joined tables; attribute-named questions => exactly those columns; dedupe bridge-join fan-out), and extend solve.py's repair gate beyond error/zero-rows to detect projection-width and duplicate-row mismatches using cheap env.execute probes, feeding the observed columns/duplicates back for a targeted second-call fix.

root_cause: Result-shape errors invisible to the execute check: drafts that run and return rows still have wrong projection width (star vs named attribute, name vs full record) or join fan-out duplicates, so the repair call is never spent
what: Add two cheap post-execution shape checks to solve.py: (a) projection-width mismatch between selected column count and attributes explicitly named in the question (catches SELECT * when one attribute is named, and single-name projections when the question asks for an entity's records), (b) duplicate rows from a fan-out join on entity-list questions (rows > DISTINCT rows), each triggering the existing second-call repair with targeted feedback and a star-projection preview; tighten prompt rules 2/6 accordingly.
decision: cost rule failed: gain -0.0333 within delta 0.0596; shaped -4.395 <= 0

root_cause: Projection/duplicate errors are invisible to the execute check: vague 'which entities' questions get narrow SELECT lists or star over joined tables, and bridge joins fan out without DISTINCT
what: Rewrite only the projection/duplicate rules in system_prompt.md: distinguish attribute-named questions (exact columns), single-entity vague questions (that entity's table.* only), multi-table 'which X ... Y' questions (SELECT * across joined tables), and add an explicit rule to use DISTINCT when joining a one-to-many bridge/enrolment table just to filter entities. This targets sp0755 (narrow Name instead of full joined rows) and sp0536 (duplicate names from enrolment fan-out) without touching control code.
